To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the optimal pension fund design can improve individual welfare, (b) age-dependent contribution rules can improve welfare of individual participants in DC pension schemes, (c) longevity risk management can improve welfare of pension fund participants.

(1) the welfare of pension fund participants is improved when the fund is organized in a collective manner, (2) a well designed age-dependent contribution rule as default in an individual DC pension scheme can improve participants' welfare substantially, and (3) the pricing of longevity risk is crucial for the risk management in pension fund.

the intergenerational risk pooling within collective pension funds can improve welfare significantly over the optimal individual risk sharing benchmark, that the optimal contribution rule for individual DC pension funds is age dependent and significantly different from the current default rule, and that the pricing of pension fund risk should take longevity into account.

the design of pension scheme and its risk management, and its impact on participants’ welfare.
the optimal design and risk sharing in funded pension schemes.
the optimal pension scheme design and its welfare implications in a life-cycle framework.
